title: Graphing a Stretched, Reflected, and Shifted Square Root
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph and analyze the function y = sqrt(1 - x / 2) by starting with the standard square root graph y = sqrt(x) and applying appropriate transformations.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = \sqrt{x} \text{ stretched horizontally by } 2,\text{ reflected across y-axis, shifted right } 2;\quad \text{Domain: } (-\infty, 2],\quad \text{Range: } [0, \infty)

steps.title: Factor the Radicand to Reveal the Horizontal Transformations
steps.explanation: Start with y = sqrt(x): (1) stretch horizontally by a factor of 2 to get y = sqrt(x/2); (2) reflect across the y-axis to get y = sqrt(-x/2); (3) shift right by 2 units by replacing x with x - 2 to get y = sqrt(-(x - 2)/2) = sqrt(1 - x/2).
steps.why: Factoring -1/2 from 1 - x/2 writes the argument in the form -(x - 2)/2.

steps.title: Determine the Domain and Range
steps.explanation: The radicand is non-negative when x <= 2, giving domain (-infinity, 2] and range [0, infinity).
steps.why: Solving 1 - x/2 >= 0 establishes the right-bounded domain (-infinity, 2].

steps.title: Find the Endpoint and Intercepts
steps.explanation: The curve has its right endpoint at (2, 0) and rises to the left through the y-intercept (0, 1) and (-6, 2).
steps.why: Evaluating at x = 2, 0, -6 gives exact integer heights.
